content.intro: Learn understanding important django files through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding Important Django Files matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines understanding important django files as part of django project structure and configuration. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: settings.py; urls.py; asgi.py; wsgi.py; manage.py; models.py , views.py , and admin.py. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: settings.py
items.text: The settings module configures installed apps, middleware, templates, databases, static files, security and other framework behavior. Keep environment-specific secrets outside committed source.

items.title: urls.py
items.text: URL configuration maps path patterns to callables and names. Use named routes and URL reversal so templates and redirects do not depend on copied hardcoded paths.

items.title: asgi.py
items.text: The ASGI entry point exposes the application through the asynchronous server interface; it matters for an ASGI deployment and does not itself make synchronous code asynchronous.

items.title: wsgi.py
items.text: The WSGI entry point exposes a synchronous application interface for compatible production servers. Choose the deployment interface supported by the application and its dependencies.

items.title: manage.py
items.text: `manage.py` sets the project settings module for management commands. Run it from the project root and the correct virtual environment.

items.title: models.py , views.py , and admin.py
items.text: models.py , views.py , and admin.py affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
